concept: A price-tag story told as a bar chart. The hero sets the known fact (10 teams since 2022) in muted grey and the reported change in bright white, with a REPORTED label in the kicker so nobody mistakes it for an announcement. Slide 2 is the hook for a business audience: one glowing gold bar for the estimated price of a 2028 franchise towering over the 2021 Lucknow and Ahmedabad bids, so the jump in value reads at a glance. Slide 3 answers 'why now' (the media-rights cycle) and ends on a city debate built for comments. Business gold, type and shapes only, no logos.
caption:
The IPL may be about to get bigger.

The BCCI is reportedly exploring two new franchises from the 2028 season, taking the league from 10 teams to 12. Nothing is official yet, and the board hasn't picked any cities.

Why 2028? That's when the next media-rights cycle begins. More teams means more matches, and more matches means a bigger rights deal.

The price tag: industry estimates cited in reports put each new team at around ₹8,800 crore. In 2021, Lucknow went for ₹7,090 crore and Ahmedabad (now Gujarat Titans) for ₹5,625 crore.

Pune, home to two past IPL sides, and Vadodara are reported to be the frontrunners.
